cues.en: a small piece of equipment called a lightning arrestor at a power plant in Odessa, Texas failed,
cues.zh: 得州 Odessa 一座发电厂里一个叫避雷器的小设备发生了故障，

cues.en: causing part of the plant to trip offline.
cues.zh: 导致电厂的一部分机组跳闸下线。

cues.en: It was a fairly typical fault that happens from time to time on the grid. There's a lot of equipment involved in producing and delivering electricity over vast distances,
cues.zh: 这是电网中时不时会发生的典型故障。要跨越很远距离生产和输送电力，涉及大量设备，

cues.en: and every once in a while, things break. Breakers isolate the problem, and we have reserves that can pick up the slack. But this fault was a little bit
cues.zh: 而设备偶尔会出问题。断路器会隔离故障，我们也有备用资源来填补缺口。但这次故障有点

cues.en: Within seconds of that one little short circuit at a power plant in Odessa, the entire Texas grid unexpectedly lost 2,500
cues.zh: 在 Odessa 一座发电厂发生那次小小的短路后几秒内，整个得州电网出人意料地损失了 2,500

cues.en: megawatts of generation capacity,
cues.zh: 兆瓦的发电容量，

cues.en: roughly 5% of the total demand, mainly from solar plants spread throughout the state. For some reason, a single 300 megawatt fault at a single power plant magnified into a loss of two and a half gigawatts
cues.zh: 约占总需求的 5%，主要来自遍布全州的太阳能电站。不知为何，一座电厂的一次 300 兆瓦故障，竟被放大成了 2.5 吉瓦的损失，

cues.en: dropping the system frequency to 59.7
cues.zh: 使系统频率降至 59.7

cues.en: hertz. The event nearly exceeded Texas's resource loss protection criteria,
cues.zh: 赫兹。这起事件几乎超出了得州的资源损失保护标准，

cues.en: which is the minimum loss of power that requires having redundancy measures in place.
cues.zh: 也就是必须采取冗余措施时所允许的最低功率损失。

cues.en: Another fault in the system could have required disconnecting customers to reduce demand. In other words, it was almost an emergency.
cues.zh: 系统中再发生一次故障，就可能需要断开部分用户来降低需求。换句话说，情况几乎进入了紧急状态。

cues.en: If you lived in Texas at the time, you probably didn't notice anything unusual, but this relatively
cues.zh: 如果当时你住在得州，可能根本没注意到任何异常，但这起相对

cues.en: innocuous event sent alarm bells ringing throughout the power industry.
cues.zh: 无害的事件却在整个电力行业敲响了警钟。

cues.en: Solar plants, large scale batteries, and wind turbines don't produce power like conventional thermal plants that make up such a big part of the grid. The investigation into the 2022
cues.zh: 太阳能电站、大规模电池储能和风力涡轮机的发电方式，都不同于在电网中占据很大比重的传统火电厂。针对 2022 年

cues.en: Odessa disturbance found that it wasn't equipment failures that caused all the solar plants to drop so much production all at once, at least not in the traditional sense.
cues.zh: Odessa 扰动事件的调查发现，并不是设备故障导致所有太阳能电站同时大幅减产，至少不是传统意义上的设备故障。

cues.en: Instead, a wide variety of algorithms and configuration
cues.zh: 相反，电力转换设备中的各种算法和配置

cues.en: settings in the power conversion equipment reacted in unexpected ways when they sensed that initial disturbance.
cues.zh: 设置在感知到最初的扰动后，以意料之外的方式做出了响应。

cues.en: The failure happened just before noon on a sunny summer day,
cues.zh: 这次故障发生在一个阳光明媚的夏日、临近中午的时候，

cues.en: so solar plants around the state were at peak output representing about 16%
cues.zh: 因此全州的太阳能电站都处于峰值输出状态，约占电网总发电量的 16%。

cues.en: of the total power generation on the grid. That might seem high, but there have already been times when solar was powering more than a third of Texas's grid, and that number is only going up. The portion of the grid comprised of solar power is climbing rapidly every year, and not just in Texas, but worldwide.
cues.zh: 这个比例看起来可能很高，但此前德州电网也曾出现过太阳能供电超过三分之一的情况，而且这个数字还在不断上升。太阳能在电网中所占的比例每年都在快速增长，而且不只是在德州，全球范围内都是如此。

cues.en: So the engineering challenges in getting these new sources of power to play nicely with the grid that wasn't really built for them are only gonna become more important. And, of course, I have some demos set up in the garage to help explain. I'm Grady, and this is Practical Engineering. In today's episode, we're talking about inverter based resources on the grid.
cues.zh: 所以，如何让这些并非为它们而建的新型电源，与电网协调运行，这些工程挑战只会变得越来越重要。当然，我还在车库里准备了一些演示，帮助大家理解这个问题。我是 Grady，这里是《Practical Engineering》。今天这一期，我们来聊聊电网中的基于逆变器的资源。

cues.en: Solar panels and batteries work on direct current, DC.
cues.zh: 太阳能板和电池使用直流电（DC）。

cues.en: If you measure the voltage coming out, it's a relatively constant number. This is actually kinda true for wind turbines as well. Of course, they are large spinning machines similar to the generators in coal or natural gas plants. But unlike in thermal power plants that can provide a smooth and consistent source of power through a steam boiler,
cues.zh: 如果你测量输出端电压，它是个相对恒定的数值。对风力涡轮机来说，这其实也大致成立。当然，它们是大型旋转机械，类似燃煤或天然气电厂里的发电机。但火电厂可以通过蒸汽锅炉提供平稳一致的电力；相比之下，

cues.en: winds vary a lot. So it's usually more efficient to let the turbine speed vary to optimize the transfer of energy from the wind into the blades. There are quite a few ways to do this, but in most cases, you get a variable speed alternating current from the turbine. Since this AC doesn't match the grid, it's easier to first convert it to DC. So you have this class of energy sources, mostly renewables, that output DC.
cues.zh: 风速变化很大。所以通常更高效的做法是让涡轮机转速变化，以优化风能向叶片的传递。实现方式有不少，但多数情况下，涡轮机输出的是变速交流电。由于这种交流电与电网不匹配，先把它转成直流电会更容易。于是就有了这一类能源：大多是可再生能源，输出直流电。

cues.en: But the grid doesn't work on DC, at least not most of it. Nearly all bulk power infrastructure,
cues.zh: 但电网并不使用直流电，至少大部分不用。几乎所有大型电力基础设施，

cues.en: including the power that makes it into your house, uses an alternating curve. I won't go into the Tesla versus Edison debate here, but the biggest benefit of an AC grid is that we can use relatively simple and inexpensive equipment,
cues.zh: 包括最终送入你家的电力，都采用交流曲线。这里不展开 Tesla 与 Edison 之争，但交流电网最大的好处是，我们可以使用相对简单且廉价的设备，

cues.en: transformers,
cues.zh: 变压器，

cues.en: to change the voltage along the way. That provides flexibility
cues.zh: 沿途改变电压。这带来了灵活性，

cues.en: between the insulation requirements and the efficiency of long distance transmission.
cues.zh: 在绝缘要求与远距离输电效率之间。

cues.en: So we have to convert, or more specifically,
cues.zh: 所以我们必须转换，更准确地说，

cues.en: invert the DC power from renewable sources onto the AC grid.
cues.zh: 是把可再生能源的直流电逆变成交流电并送入电网。

cues.en: In fact, batteries, solar panels, and most wind turbines are collectively known to power professionals as inverter based resources
cues.zh: 事实上，电池、太阳能板和大多数风力涡轮机，被电力专业人士统称为逆变器型资源

cues.en: because they're so different from their counterparts.
cues.zh: 因为它们与同类设备差别太大了。

cues.en: Here's why.
cues.zh: 原因如下。

cues.en: The oldest inverters were mechanical devices, a motor connected to a generator. This is pretty simple to show. I have a battery powered drill coupled to a synchronous motor. When I pull the trigger, the drill motor spins the synchronous motor, generating a nice sine wave we can see on the oscilloscope.
cues.zh: 最早的逆变器是机械装置：一台电动机连着一台发电机。这个演示起来很简单。我有一台电池供电的电钻，连着一台同步电机。我一扣扳机，电钻的电机就带动同步电机旋转，产生一个漂亮的正弦波，我们可以在示波器上看到。

cues.en: Maybe you can see the disadvantages here. For one, this is not very efficient.
cues.zh: 也许你能看出这里的缺点。首先，这效率不高。

cues.en: There are losses in each step of converting electricity to mechanical energy and then back into electrical energy on the other side. Also, the frequency depends on the speed of the motor, which is not always a simple matter to control. So these days, most inverters use solid state electronic circuits.
cues.zh: 电能先转成机械能、再在另一端转回电能，每一步都有损耗。而且频率取决于电机转速，而转速并不总是容易控制。所以如今，大多数逆变器使用固态电子电路。

cues.en: And look what I found in my garage.
cues.zh: 看看我在车库里找到了什么。

cues.en: These are practically ubiquitous these days partly because cars use a DC system, and it's convenient to power AC devices from them. I just hook it up to the battery and get nice clean power from the other end.
cues.zh: 它们如今几乎无处不在，部分原因是汽车使用直流系统，用它们给交流设备供电很方便。我只要把它接到电池上，另一端就能输出干净漂亮的电。

cues.en: Just kidding. These cheap inverters definitely output alternating current, but often in a way that barely resembles a sine wave. Connecting a load to the device moves it out a bit, but not much.
cues.zh: 开个玩笑。这些廉价逆变器确实输出交流电，但波形往往几乎不像正弦波。接上负载会让波形稍微好一点，但也好不了多少。

cues.en: That's because of what's happening under the hood. In essence, switches in the inverter turn on and off, creating pulses of power. By controlling the timing of the pulses, you can adjust the average current flowing out of the inverter to swing up and down into an approximate sine wave. Cheaper inverters just use a few switches to create a roughly wave like signal.
cues.zh: 这是因为底层发生的过程。本质上，逆变器里的开关不断通断，产生功率脉冲。通过控制脉冲的时序，可以调节逆变器输出的平均电流上下摆动，形成近似正弦波。更便宜的逆变器只用几个开关，产生大致类似波形的信号。

cues.en: More sophisticated inverters can flip the switches much more quickly, smoothing the curve into something closer to a sine wave. This is called pulse width modulation.
cues.zh: 更复杂的逆变器能让开关切换得快得多，把曲线平滑到更接近正弦波。这叫做脉宽调制。

cues.en: Boost the voltage on the way in or the way out, add some filters to smooth out the choppiness of the pulses, and that's how you get a battery to run an AC device. But it's not quite how you get a solar panel to send power into the grid. There's a lot more to this equipment.
cues.zh: 在输入端或输出端升压，再加一些滤波器来平滑脉冲的毛刺，这样就能让电池驱动交流设备。但这还不是让太阳能板向电网送电的方式。这类设备要复杂得多。

cues.en: For one, look at the waveform of my inverter and the one from the grid. They're similar enough,
cues.zh: 首先，看看我的逆变器波形和电网波形。它们已经足够相似，

cues.en: but they're definitely not a match. Even the frequency is a little bit off. I will not be making an interconnection here since I don't have a permit from the utility, but even if I did, this inverter would let out the magic smoke. A grid tie inverter has to be able to both synchronize with the phase and frequency of the grid and be able to vary the voltage of the waveform to control how much current is flowing into or out of the device.
cues.zh: 但两者绝对不匹配。连频率都差了一点。我不会在这里做并网连接，因为我没有电力公司的许可；但即使有，这台逆变器也会冒出 magic smoke。并网逆变器必须既能与电网的相位和频率同步，又能调节波形电压，以控制流入或流出设备的电流大小。

cues.en: The synchronization part often involves a circuit called a phase locked loop. The inverter senses the voltage of the grid and sets the timing of all those little switches accordingly to match what it sees. So these are often called grid following inverters.
cues.zh: 同步部分通常涉及一种叫做锁相环的电路。逆变器检测电网电压，并根据检测到的电压来设定所有那些小开关的时序，使其与之匹配。所以这些通常被称为跟网型逆变器。

cues.en: They synchronize to the grid frequency and phase and only vary the voltage to control the flow of power. And that hints at one of their challenges,
cues.zh: 它们同步到电网的频率和相位，只通过改变电压来控制功率流动。这也暗示了它们面临的挑战之一，

cues.en: they only work when the grid is up.
cues.zh: 它们只有在电网正常运行时才能工作。

cues.en: I've done a video all about black starts, so check that out after this if you wanna learn more. But in general,
cues.zh: 我做过一个关于黑启动的视频，如果想了解更多，看完这个可以去看那个。但总的来说，

cues.en: inverter based resources like solar, wind, and batteries can only follow what's already on the grid. When the system's down, they are too, regardless of whether the sun's shining or the wind's blowing. That's why most grid tied solar systems on houses can't give you power during an outage. There's another interesting thing that inverters do for solar panels, and I can show you how it works in my driveway.
cues.zh: 基于逆变器的资源，如太阳能、风能和电池，只能跟随电网上已有的东西。当系统瘫痪时，它们也瘫痪了，不管太阳是否照耀或风是否吹拂。这就是为什么大多数并网家用太阳能系统在停电时无法供电。逆变器对太阳能面板还有另一个有趣的作用，我可以在我的车道上演示给你们看。

cues.en: I have a solar panel hooked up to a variable resistor, and I'm measuring voltage and current produced by the panel. You can see as I lower the resistance, the output voltage of the panel goes down, and the current supplies goes up. But this isn't a linear effect.
cues.zh: 我把一块太阳能面板接在一个可变电阻上，测量面板产生的电压和电流。可以看到，当我降低电阻时，面板的输出电压下降，而电流上升。但这不是线性效应。

cues.en: I recorded the voltage and current over the full range and multiplied them together to get the power output. If you graph the power as a function of voltage, you get this shape, and you can see there's an optimum resistance that gets you the most power out of the panel. It's called the maximum power point. If you deviate on either side of it, you get less power out. In other words, you're leaving power on the tape. You're not taking full advantage of the panel's capacity. What's even more challenging is that point changes depending on the temperature of the panel and the amount of sun hitting it. I ran this test again with a few more clouds, and you can see how the graph changes.
cues.zh: 我记录了整个范围内的电压和电流，并将它们相乘得到功率输出。如果把功率作为电压的函数画成图，就得到这个形状，可以看到存在一个最佳电阻值，能让面板输出最大功率。这被称为最大功率点。如果偏离这个点任何一侧，输出功率都会减少。换句话说，你在浪费功率。你没有充分利用面板的容量。更具挑战性的是，这个点会随面板温度和日照量而变化。我在云多一些的时候又做了一次测试，可以看到图表是如何变化的。

cues.en: So nearly all large solar photovoltaic
cues.zh: 几乎所有大型太阳能光伏

cues.en: installations use what's called a maximum power point tracker or MPPT
cues.zh: 装置都使用所谓的最大功率点跟踪器，简称MPPT

cues.en: that essentially adjusts the resistance to follow that point as it changes with sunniness and temperature. It's really a separate device from the inverter, but often they're located right next to each other and inside the same housing. Even this panel came with a charge controller that has this MPPT function, and you can see it adjusting the flow of current to constantly try and stay at the peak of the curve while it charges this battery. These can be used for an entire installation, but in many cases, each panel or group of panels gets its own MPPT
cues.zh: 它本质上是通过调节电阻来跟随那个随日照和温度变化的功率点。它其实是跟逆变器分开的设备，但通常两者紧挨着放在同一个外壳里。就连这块板子也自带一个具备MPPT功能的充电控制器，你可以看到它在调节电流，在给电池充电的同时不断试图保持在曲线的峰值。这些可以用于整个装置，但很多情况下，每块板或每组板都有各自的MPPT

cues.en: because that curve is just a little bit different for each one. Tracking the peak power output individually
cues.zh: 因为每块板的曲线都略有不同。单独跟踪每块的峰值功率输出

cues.en: can often squeeze a little more capacity out of the system.
cues.zh: 往往能从系统中多榨出一点容量。

cues.en: Squeezing out capacity is essential to address another challenge associated with inverter based resources on the grid, frequency.
cues.zh: 榨出容量对于应对并网逆变器类资源的另一个挑战至关重要，那就是频率。

cues.en: The rate at which the voltage and current on the grid swing back and forth is an important measure of how well generation and demand are balanced. If demand outstrips the generation capacity,
cues.zh: 电网电压和电流来回摆动的频率，是衡量发电与需求平衡程度的重要指标。如果需求超过发电容量，

cues.en: the frequency of the grid slows down. Lots of equipment, both on the generation side and the stuff we plug in, is designed to rely on a stable grid frequency. So if it deviates too far, stuff goes wrong. Devices malfunction,
cues.zh: 电网频率就会下降。很多设备，无论是发电侧的还是我们插电使用的，都依赖稳定的电网频率。所以一旦偏离太多，就会出问题。设备会故障，

cues.en: motors can overheat,
cues.zh: 电机会过热，

cues.en: generators get out of sync, and more. It's so important that rather than let the frequency get too far out of whack, grid operators will disconnect customers to get electrical demands back in balance with the available supply of power called an under frequency load shed. Things go wrong on the grid all the time, so generators have to be able to make up for contingencies to keep the frequency stable.
cues.zh: 发电机会失去同步，等等。正因如此重要，电网运营商会宁可断开部分用户，让电力需求与可用供电重新平衡，而不是让频率偏离太远，这叫低频减载。电网随时都会出问题，所以发电机必须能够弥补突发状况，以保持频率稳定。

cues.en: Here's the quintessential
cues.zh: 这就是最典型的例子

cues.en: example, an unexpected loss of generation.
cues.zh: 发电量意外损失的例子。

cues.en: Say a generator trips offline,
cues.zh: 假设一台发电机突然离线，

cues.en: maybe because of a failed lightning arrestor like the Odessa example.
cues.zh: 可能是因为避雷器故障，就像 Odessa 的例子一样。

cues.en: The system frequency immediately starts dropping since power demand now exceeds the generation,
cues.zh: 由于电力需求超过了当前发电量，系统频率会立即开始下降，

cues.en: and the frequency will keep dropping unless we inject more power into the system. The first part of that, called primary frequency response, usually comes from automatic governors in power plants. If we do it fast enough, the frequency will reach a low point called the nadir and then recover to the nominal value. The nadir is a critical point because if it gets too low, the grid will have to shed load in order to recover. The other important value is called the rate of change of frequency,
cues.zh: 除非我们向系统注入更多电力，否则频率会持续下降。这个过程的第一阶段称为一次调频，通常由发电厂中的自动调速器负责。如果响应足够快，频率会降到一个最低点，也就是频率最低点，然后恢复到额定值。频率最低点非常关键，因为如果它降得太低，电网就必须切除负荷才能恢复。另一个重要指标叫作频率变化率，

cues.en: basically the slope of this line. It determines how much time is available to get more power into the system before the frequency gets too low, and there are several factors that play into it. How much generation was lost in the first place? How quickly can we respond? And how much inertia
cues.zh: 基本上就是这条线的斜率。它决定了在频率过低之前，我们有多少时间向系统注入更多电力，而影响它的因素有很多。最初损失了多少发电量？我们能多快做出响应？以及电网上有多少惯量

cues.en: there is on the grid? Thermal power plants that traditionally make up the bulk of generating capacity are gigantic spinning machines. They're basically a bunch of synchronized flywheels.
cues.zh: 传统上构成主要发电能力的火电厂，都是巨大的旋转机械。它们基本上就是一组同步运行的飞轮。

cues.en: That kinetic energy helps keep them spinning during a disturbance, reducing the slope of the frequency during an unexpected loss. Maybe you can see a problem with a simple grid following inverter. It's locked in phase with the frequency even if that frequency is wrong,
cues.zh: 这些动能有助于它们在发生扰动时继续旋转，从而减小意外损失发生时的频率变化率。你可能已经看出简单的跟网型逆变器存在什么问题了。它会锁定在系统频率的相位上，即使这个频率是错误的，

cues.en: and it has no physical inertia to help arrest a deviation in frequency.
cues.zh: 而且它没有物理惯量来帮助抑制频率偏差。

cues.en: If we keep everything the same and just increase the share of inverter based resources,
cues.zh: 如果我们保持一切不变，只是增加基于逆变器的资源占比，

cues.en: any loss of generation will mean a steeper slope, reducing the time available to get backup supplies onto the grid before it's forced to shed load. Larger renewable plants like solar and wind farms are increasingly required to participate in primary frequency response,
cues.zh: 那么任何发电损失都意味着更陡的斜率，从而缩短了在被迫切负荷之前将备用电源接入电网的时间。像太阳能和风电场这样的大型可再生能源电站，越来越多地被要求参与一次频率响应，

cues.en: injecting power into the grid immediately when the frequency drops. And some inverters can even create synthetic inertia that mimics a turbine's physical response to changes in frequency.
cues.zh: 在频率下降时立即向电网注入功率。而一些逆变器甚至可以产生合成惯性，模拟涡轮机对频率变化的物理响应。

cues.en: But there's another challenge to this. Dealing with an over frequency event is relatively straightforward.
cues.zh: 但这里还有另一个挑战。应对过频事件相对简单。

cues.en: Just reduce the amount of energy you're sending into the grid. But response to an under frequency event requires you to have more energy to inject. In other words, you have to run the plant below its maximum capacity just in case it gets called on during an unexpected loss somewhere else in the system. For a power company,
cues.zh: 只需减少送入电网的能量即可。但应对欠频事件则要求你有更多能量可以注入。换句话说，你必须让电站低于最大容量运行，以防系统中其他地方发生意外损失时被调用。对电力公司来说，

cues.en: that means leaving money on the table. So in most places, the energy markets are set up to pay power plants to maintain a certain level of reserve capacity
cues.zh: 这意味着白白放弃收入。所以在大多数地方，能源市场的设计是向电厂付费以维持一定水平的备用容量，

cues.en: either through operating below maximum output or including battery storage in the plant. The last big thing that inverter based resources have to manage is faults.
cues.zh: 要么通过低于最大出力运行，要么通过在电站中加入电池储能。基于逆变器的资源必须应对的最后一个大问题是故障。

cues.en: Of course, you need protective systems that can de energize solar or wind resources when conditions on the grid could lead to damage. These are expensive projects, and there's almost no limit to the things that can go wrong requiring costly repairs or replacement.
cues.zh: 当然，你需要保护系统，在电网条件可能导致损坏时能够切断太阳能或风能资源。这些是昂贵的项目，而且几乎没有什么故障是不可能发生的，需要 costly 的维修或更换。

cues.en: But for the stability of the grid, you can't have those protective systems being so sensitive that they trip at the hint of something unusual like what happened in Odessa.
cues.zh: 但为了电网的稳定性，你不能让这些保护系统的敏感度高到只要有一点异常苗头就跳闸，就像敖德萨发生的那样。

cues.en: This concept is usually referred to as a ride through. Especially for under frequency events, you need inverters to continue supplying power to the grid to provide support. If they trip offline or even reduce power in response to a disturbance,
cues.zh: 这个概念通常被称为低电压穿越（或不间断运行）。特别是对于低频事件，你需要逆变器继续向电网供电以提供支持。如果它们因应对扰动而离网跳闸甚至降低功率，

cues.en: it can lead to a cascading outage. This is kind of a tug of war between owners trying to protect their equipment and grid operators saying, hey. Faults happen, and we need you to not shut the whole system down when they do. And reliability requirements are getting more specific as the equipment evolves because every manufacturer has their own flavor of protective settings and algorithms.
cues.zh: 这可能会导致级联停电。这有点像是一场拉锯战：一方面是试图保护设备的业主，另一方面是电网运营商，他们说：故障时有发生，当故障发生时，我们需要你们不要关闭整个系统。随着设备的演进，可靠性要求变得越来越具体，因为每个制造商都有自己的一套保护设置和算法。

cues.en: As inverter based resources continue to grow rapidly in proportion to the overall generation portfolio,
cues.zh: 随着基于逆变器的电源在整体发电结构中的比例继续快速增长，

cues.en: their engineering challenges are only becoming more important. We talked about a few of the big ones, lack of black startability,
cues.zh: 它们的工程挑战变得愈发重要。我们讨论了其中几个重大挑战：缺乏黑启动能力、

cues.en: low inertia, and performance during disturbances.
cues.zh: 低惯量，以及在扰动期间的性能。

cues.en: And there are a lot more. But inverters also provide a lot of opportunities.
cues.zh: 还有很多其他的挑战。但逆变器也带来了许多机遇。

cues.en: They're really powerful devices and the technology is improving quickly.
cues.zh: 它们是非常强大的设备，而且这项技术正在快速改进。

cues.en: They can chop up power basically however you want, and they aren't constrained by the physical limitations of large generating plants.
cues.zh: 它们基本上可以随心所欲地切割电力，并且不受大型发电厂物理限制的约束。

cues.en: So they can respond more quickly, and unlike physical inertia that will eventually peter out, inverters can provide a sustained response.
cues.zh: 这样它们就能更快响应，而且不同于最终会逐渐消失的物理惯性，逆变器可以提供持续的响应。

cues.en: There are even grid forming inverters that, unlike their grid following brethren, can black start or support an isolated island without the need for a functioning grid to rely on. We're in the growing pain stage right now working out the bugs that these new types of energy generation create. But if you pay attention to what's happening in the industry, it's mostly good news. A lot of people from all sides of the industry are working really hard on these engineering challenges so that we'll soon come out with a more reliable,
cues.zh: 甚至还有构网型逆变器，与它们跟网型的同类不同，可以在没有可运行电网依赖的情况下实现黑启动或支持孤岛运行。我们现在正处于成长的阵痛阶段，正在解决这些新型能源发电方式带来的问题。但如果你关注行业动态，大多是好消息。来自行业各方的人们都在非常努力地应对这些工程挑战，以便我们很快能拿出一个更可靠、

cues.en: sustainable,
cues.zh: 可持续、

cues.en: and resilient grid on the other end.
cues.zh: 且更有韧性的电网。

cues.en: I build a lot of homemade demonstrations for videos like this one, and I hope it comes across how much joy it gives me. I love the challenge of making something useful with constraints on budget and tools, but I've never built a hot air balloon. One of my fellow creators who runs the Neo channel just released a video on this incredible story of two families escaping East Germany in maybe the most creative way possible.
cues.zh: 我为这样的视频制作了很多自制演示，我希望你能感受到这给我带来了多大的快乐。我喜欢在预算和工具受限的情况下做出有用东西的挑战，但我从没造过热气球。我的一位创作者同行，运营Neo频道的，刚发布了一个视频，讲的是两个家庭以可能是最有创意的方式逃离东德的不可思议的故事。

cues.zh: 我不知道你怎样，但我得说，如今我看的几乎一切都是独立创作者制作的。那些不必经过五层制片厂高管才能问世的内容，就是有一种真正的真实感和原创性。

cues.zh: Neo 关于气球逃生的那一期就是一个完美的例子，这是一个关于自制工程学的迷人故事，

cues.zh: 其中还包括对其中一位尝试者的采访，

cues.zh: 配上他们标志性的精美动画。如果你想看的话，它只在 Nebula 上独家播映。

cues.zh: 即使你现在还没订阅，大概也听说过 Nebula 了。这是一个由独立创作者创立、为独立创作者服务的流媒体服务。

cues.en: No studio executives deciding what gets the green light, no algorithm deriving the content into a single style,
cues.zh: 没有高管来决定什么项目能通过，没有算法把内容变成千篇一律的风格，

cues.en: and no ads getting in the way. We just released a huge update that completely redesigned the homepage,
cues.zh: 也没有广告从中捣乱。我们刚刚发布了一次重大更新，彻底重新设计了主页，

There's tons of originals and we're always adding creators so the new categories can help you discover content related to your interests. My videos go live on Nebula before they come out here and my practical construction series where I embedded on a construction site for a year was specifically produced for Nebula viewers who want to see deeper dives into specific topics.
cues.zh: 让你在关注的最爱之外，能更轻松地发现新内容。这里有大量的原创作品，而且我们一直在添加新的创作者，所以新的分类能帮你发现符合你兴趣的内容。我的视频在 Nebula 上线的时间会比这里早，而我的实地建造系列——我深入建筑工地呆了一年——就是专门为那些想要深入了解特定主题的 Nebula 观众制作的。
